sentences.text:
This claim petition is filed U/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.
2.

The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 09.04.2024 at about 16.15 to 6.20 p.m, when the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-66-H-5222 by following all the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near V.L.Nagara Flyover, on NH-69 service road,
Thangli Village, Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District, at that time one car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-P-1274 which was driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner on opposite direction so as to endanger the human life and dashed the deceased's motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident he was rushed to Kaduru Government Hospital, wherein the duty doctors who examined him declared as he was brought dead.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of car.
The respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Inspite of due service of the notice of petition, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 filed objections statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

Non -compliance of section 134(c),
158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence,
mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the public place by consuming alcohol and the deceased was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident
. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES

near V.L.Nagara Flyover, on NH-69 service road, Thangli Village, Kadur Taluk,
Chikkamagaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-11-P-1274 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. The Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1. Ex's.
P1 to 23 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined the employer of deceased as PW.2 and through him Ex.P.24 to 33 were marked.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondents on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2: The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending car.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.
9. Mr.Gangadharappa.
T set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.13) against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. Further the learned counsel for the Insurance Company vehemently argued that as the deceased was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet, contributory negligence must be attributed to him.
The mere fact that at the time of accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, he can held be guilty of being a party to the violation of law.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Swathi M vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67160798/
3 Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammad Siddique & another V/s National Insurance Company Ltd & others), such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence.

sentences.text: 11. The respondent No.2 failed to appear despite due service of notice of the petition upon him.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
Though the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.

With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of petitioners and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, either in the police records or petition, no where mentioned about the parents of the deceased Mallikarjuna.

C.N. 
Therefore for clarification when asked about the same to the counsel for petitioners, the petitioners counsel filed memo by stating that parents of the deceased Mallikarjuna died prior to the death of Mallikarjuna C.N. Hence the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the claimants is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, claimants are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.3 : LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card and DL to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P17 & 18, wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 08.06.1980, which indicates that he was aged (43 years 10 months 1 days) 44 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '14'.
14.

In order to substantiate the fact the deceased was working as a Police Constable, Kadur Police Station, Chickmagalur, Government of Karnataka and drawing salary of Rs.61,699/- p.m, the petitioners have produced Appointment letter, Salary slips, Bank Statement and Form No.16 at Ex.P.20 to 23 and also got examined the Assistant Administrative Officer, SP Office,
Chikkamagaluru as PW.2.

This witness produced the certified copy of Appointment letter, Service Register, Promotion order, Service Register Extract, Memo, Salary slips and Form No.16 for the year 2022-23, 2023-2024 and 2024-25 of deceased which are exhibited at ExP.26 to 33.
On perusal of Ex.P.32 pay slips it discloses that deceased was getting salary of Rs.61,699/- in the month of March-2024 and a sum of Rs.19,494/- in the month of April-2024.
The testimony of this witness which is fortified by the said exhibit was not displaced during cross-examination.
15. Generally it is the last drawn salary that needs to be taken into consideration for the calculation of compensation.

But in this case as the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road Swathi M vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67160798/
4 traffic accident that occurred on 09.04.2024, he worked only for 8 days in the month of April- 2024.

sentences.text: Therefore the last month salary i.e., for the month of March-2024 is considered for determining the compensation.
As per Ex.P.23 his income for April-2024 cannot be considered for determining compensation.
Further during April-2024, the deceased's pay was calculated for 9 days and in the said document they paid Rs.19,494/- after death to his LR's.
Therefore, in the March-2024 pay slip the deceased's pay was calculated for 31 days and in the said document they paid Rs.61,699/-.
Hence his salary for the last full worked month i.e., March-2024 is taken into account for computing the dependency compensation.
The gross salary of the deceased for the said month is Rs.61,699/-.
On perusal of Ex.P.33 being the Form No.16, which discloses that the deceased was not income tax payee.
As such the gross salary of deceased is considered as Rs.61,699/-.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi and others, except income tax no deduction is to be made from the salary of the deceased qua other allowances.

sentences.text: Even otherwise from the elicitation brought out during the course of cross-examination of PW.2 it is crystal clear at after the death of deceased, death benefits has been paid to petitioner No.1 and apart from this, the first applicant was given a job on compassionate grounds.
16. Be that as it may, annual income works out to Rs.7,40,388/- (Rs.61,699 X 12).
Out of the said annual income, professional tax and income tax needs to be deducted.
The calculation table for which stands as follows :

Annual Gross Salary 7,40,388  (Rs.61,699 x12)
 Annual Professional Tax (less) 2,400  Total 7,37,988  Less Tax Exemption 2,50,000  (for the assessment year 2023-  2024- FY-2024-2025)

Taxable Income 4,87,988  Tax payable @ 5% on 24,400  Rs.4,87,988/- (during the year  2023)
 Gross Income 7,40,388  Less Total Tax payable 26,800  (2,400 + 24,400 =12,086)
 Annual Established Income 7,13,588  Monthly Established Income 59,466  (7,13,588 / 12)
17.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 44 years.
His income is taken as Rs.59,466/- p.m.
In this case the deceased being an employee of the State Government had a permanent job.
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 30% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
30% of Rs.59,466/- works out to Rs.17,840/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.77,306/- (59,466 + 17,840).
There are three dependents.
Hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
1/3rd of Rs.77,306/- works out to Rs.25,768/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.51,538/- (77,306 - 25,768).
Annual income works out to Rs.6,18,456/- (51,538 X 12).

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.86,58,384/- (Rs.6,18,456 X 14) which is rounded off to Rs.86,58,400/-.
18.

Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
19.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and parents as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a mother/father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father/mother.
Therefore, petitioners No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

20. The calculation table stands as follows :

21 . REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.88,23,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Petitioner No.3 - 30% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer & printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 3rd day of December -2025).

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.88,23,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Petitioner No.3 - 30% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
